move: screenshots spring from a centre pile into a grid, tilt, pile back
how: Eight 200x300 phone screenshots in a 4-column grid all start collapsed on the frame centre (x/y offsets computed from getBoundingClientRect toward 640,360), fanned rotate (i-3.5)*4deg, scale 0.7, opacity 0, 40px low. Each springs to its grid cell with 0.9s back.out(1.4), staggered 0.07s from 3% of the 3s duration; a caption fades in at 30%. The whole grid tilts rotateX -6 / rotateY 6 with sine.inOut from 33% to 73% then returns. From 83% the shots fly back to the centre in reverse order (0.04s stagger), scale 0.7, opacity 0, 40px high, with power3.in, and the caption fades, so the frame ends empty as it began.
adapt: Replace the eight screen names and hero gradients (or use real screenshots), the caption and the dark-index rule; change grid columns for a different count. Keep the 0.9s back.out(1.4) spring with 0.07s stagger.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the grid from shot.screens; animate(el, shot, D) returns the timeline with entries at (0.033 + i*0.023)*D, tilt at 0.33D and gather at 0.83D. The centre-offset maths uses getBoundingClientRect against a hard-coded 640,360 viewport centre, so replace it with offsets relative to el's own rect (or rely on the grid's translate(-50%,-50%) and compute from cell index).
caveats: centre offsets assume a 1280x720 viewport via getBoundingClientRect; must be measured relative to the container when ported
loop closes visually: both end frames are empty, though the final pile sits 40px above the initial one
